decisions.reason: As a peripheral consumer product with only modest public commitment and no centrality to the firm's announced direction, management perceives little sunk cost or need for justification, making a drop more likely.

As a core waste-to-energy line with multiple models, it encapsulates significant investment and customer commitments, so escalation of commitment inclines management to keep it despite any temporary setbacks.

As a publicly launched flagship with quantified promotion and central to the firm's direction, dropping it would write off a major investment and publicly expose the earlier decision as a mistake, so escalation strongly favors keeping it.
As a flagship focus close to the core with visible commitment, management will persist because of sunk costs and the need to justify the public commitment.
